content: Several studies have shown that NLI datasets like SNLI BIBREF14 and MultiNLI BIBREF15 contain spurious patterns that can be exploited to obtain strong results without making real inferential decisions. For instance, BIBREF16 and BIBREF17 showed that a hypothesis-only baseline performs better than chance due to cues on their lexical choice and sentence length. Similarly, BIBREF18 showed that NLI models tend to predict entailment for sentence pairs with a high lexical overlap. Several authors have worked on adversarial datasets to diagnose these issues and provide a more challenging benchmark BIBREF19, BIBREF20, BIBREF21. Besides NLI, other tasks like QA have also been found to be susceptible to annotation artifacts BIBREF22, BIBREF23. While previous work has focused on the monolingual scenario, we show that translation can interfere with these artifacts in multilingual settings.
